::: {.why}
Every capacity figure you have reported since week 25 rested on an assumed exponent and an assumed coefficient, and today both are measurements, which will move the numbers downward.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report revised capacity for every signal in the book, with the change from the assumed model quantified.
- State which assumption drove most of the change.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Produce the revision table: for each signal, old and new capacity in dollars, and the change attributed between the exponent, the coefficient and the volatility scaling. Attributing the change is more useful than reporting it, because it tells you which measurement to improve next.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Recompute the combined book's capacity, which is not the sum of the parts: signals that trade the same names compete for the same liquidity, so the book's capacity is below the sum and the shortfall depends on the overlap. Compute the overlap explicitly from the position vectors rather than assuming independence.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Every capacity figure in the alpha book is recomputed from the fitted impact model, and the combined book's capacity accounts for signals competing for the same liquidity rather than being the sum of the parts.
:::

## Resources

- [Tóth et al. (2011) — Anomalous price impact and the critical nature of liquidity](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.1694) [paper]{.res-kind}
- [Amihud (2002) — Illiquidity and stock returns](https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~mkearns/finread/amihud.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
The capacity revision table with the change attributed, plus a combined-book capacity that accounts for position overlap.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your book's capacity is below the sum of its signals' capacities. By how much, and what did you compute to find out?
:::
